overall: The AG found the Board deliberated outside a posted meeting by email on July 7 when the chair forwarded a member's email to a third member, ordered future compliance and release of the email chain, and found no other violation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board deliberated outside a posted meeting about reducing Conservation Commission membership and reappointing members.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board deliberated outside of notice meeting on July 7 when Mr. Fill forwarded Ms. Nevinsmith’s email regarding the Board’s authority to reduce the size of the Commission to Mr. Waskiewicz, thus causing the communication to reach a quorum of the Board.

allegations.summary: Alleged a July 6 phone call and other private communications among members deliberated the Commission membership decision outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Although we are concerned that the Board may have further discussed the membership of the Commission, following our investigation, we were unable to find sufficient evidence of improper deliberation.

allegations.summary: Complainant contested whether the Board was authorized to reduce Commission membership and decline reappointment; this was outside the review's scope.
allegations.key_passage: we do not review, and take no position on, whether the Board was authorized to or justified in reducing the number of Commission members and not reappointing Ms. Kuzdeba.

remedy: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
We order the Board, if it has not already done so, to release to the public the full chain of July 7 emails.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law and may result in the imposition of $1,000 civil penalty per intentional violation.
